lines.en: Osako helps me back up and, after taking a moment or two to remember who I am, where I am, and the reason I came here, we exit the dojo and begin to head to-
: Osako, where are we going?
: I’m kidnapping you.
: Why? No one’s going to want to buy a washed-up creep in his early 30s off of you.
: I’m sure Ayane would pay. Maybe even that other girl who was thinking about buying the dojo way back when. I don’t know. I’ll find out later.
Okay, so I guess I’m being kidnapped.
If I had known this was coming at the time of my departure, I would have noted something about my disappearance in my letter to-
Actually, haven’t I already crossed this line of thinking once today?
: I think you might have given me brain damage.
: Is that a good thing or a bad thing? Because you seem a little less miserable than you were a few minutes ago. Maybe I kicked the sadness out of you?
: Maybe. Let me think about it for a second.
: Nope. I’m still overflowing with pain. And now I also have to worry about the living conditions in whatever warehouse you’re going to stash my body in until you can find a buyer. So thanks.
: Damn. I’ll have to kick you a little bit harder next time.
: Where are we going? For real. Because I have to get back home soon.
: Isn’t your niece in high school? Why can’t she go a few hours without parental supervision?
: Because her hair is short now.
: What? So is mine and I look after myself all the time.
: It’s complicated. Just tell me where-
: Food. I think I owe you a meal after almost killing you. Plus, being so much stronger than you really worked up an appetite on my end.
: I think you’re taking more pleasure in my misery than you’re supposed to. Everyone else has been very sensitive and understanding and you’re too busy leveraging your strength to even care.
: Yeah. I guess I just hate you, then. Where do you want to eat?
: Next to someone who won’t hurt me.
: How about here? Here looks good.
Osako drags me into an American style diner that is so authentic I can barely make out any of the menu items as they’re all in English.
: Why here? Why would you say this looks good?
: Because you would have just cried for the next ten minutes instead of deliberating. Plus, I’m used to Wakana never knowing where to eat and have decided to just start picking the first thing I see.
: It’s a strategy that’s yet to let me down. But I’m anticipating an end to that streak today as it seems like you’re out to ruin everything you come across.
: I’m not out to do that. It’s just a side effect of my existence.
: Well, whatever it is, cut it out. Because you had your turn to complain and now its mine.
: I think I deserve more time to complain as I don’t get to do it very often and you do it virtually every time Wakana looks at you the wrong way.
: And more recently, when she doesn’t look at me at all!
: You seem unusually...jubilant for someone who is about to spill their heart out.
: I kind of have to be. If we both spend the whole afternoon moaning, the wait staff will-
: Think we’re having heterosexual sex?
: I was going to say “kick us out.” But yours is way worse and I’d like to avoid anyone thinking that at any and all costs.
: I like having a lesbian friend who says degrading things to me. This is the most fun I’ve had since the last time I told you this was the most fun I’ve had roughly thirty minutes ago.
: You really are a masochist, huh?
: A verbal one, I guess. I’d get soft if you slapped me.
: Are you saying it’s hard right now?
: Hard to be alive.
: Okay. Well, I’m gonna go grab a table.
: And I’m going to stand here until my feet fuse with the tiles and my legs need to be amputated in order to get me to leave.
: Please don’t do that, sir. We’re understaffed as it is.
: I’m sorry, but this is the fate that I’ve chosen for myself.
: Okay. Come on, Grandpa. Let’s get you into your chair.
: Why does everything have to hurt so much?
: Forgive him. He’s very old. He just looks young because he...eats well.
: Help. She abuses me when no one is around and won’t listen to my problems.
: God, I need a new job...
We grab a seat near the window instead of one at the bar as I’d rather be dyed gold by the setting sun than painted black by the intangible arms of the words I will soon spit out.
Osako orders a hamburg steak. I order nothing.
She doesn’t like that, so she orders a pork cutlet set and then slides it over to me once it arrives several minutes later.
I’ve been trying to avoid good food as Ami doesn’t get to have any and it seems wrong for me to partake in one of the pleasures of life while she can not.
I’m sure everything would just taste grey to her right now anyway, though.
I hope she recovers soon. And not just because it will free up some more time in my schedule and my mind.
But because I love her.
I really do love her.
And it’s my fault she’s like this.
: Are you really gonna sit there and frown for the entire meal? I bought you food. Eat it.
: Can we just get the sad part out of the way first? Because I really don’t want to take a bite out of this if you’re going to get all self-loathing a few seconds in and cause me to stop.
: Oh, shut up. I am going to complain, but it’s actually not about me this time. I’m perfectly normal and perfectly fine.
: Well, way to rub it in.
: There’s no winning with you when you’re like this, is there?
: Probably not, no.
: Pfft. I see now why Wakana likes you so much.
: You’re actually really similar in a lot of ways. And I’d wager she’s even more stubborn than you are.
: You’d probably lose, then. Because at least Wakana was willing to change some of what she was doing to appease you.
: Change what she was doing to appease me? But what did-
: Oh! You’re probably talking about the medication, aren’t you? Yeah. She’s gotten a lot more responsible after I talked to her about that stuff.
: But I feel like that’s less “being stubborn” and more “Hey, I probably shouldn’t die right now.” Regardless of her catch phrase, of course.
: Well, there’s one thing to cross off the similarity list because I definitely-
: If you talk about how you want to die one more time today, I am going to take these chopsticks and insert them into your eyes. Then, I am going to eat your eyes. Then, you won’t have eyes anymore.
: Is that really the path you want to go down? One without eyes?
: It would definitely make not giving into temptation easier.
: God, it’s like talking to a big, ugly wall.
: You’re only saying that because you’re scared of penises.
: Well sorry for not being attracted to your weird, fleshy sex-tumor with the capability of shooting out liquid babies.
: Apology accepted. Enjoy your equally fleshy meat-pocket that real babies crawl out of.
: Never call it a meat-pocket again.
: I’m sorry. But on the bright side, I think that’s the closest I’ve come to making a joke since coming out of my coma.
: You call that a joke?
: Somewhat reluctantly, yes.
: So, you were comparing me to the woman you have sex with?
: Somewhat reluctantly, yes.
: You see...
: Apart from the fact that you’re both stubborn teachers with...fatalistic tendencies and other assorted mental issues, you’re both kind of...caught up on the same thing right now.
: I have a very hard time believing that Wakana is going through something even remotely similar to what I’m going through as the only thing she loves is sitting directly in front of me.
: No, I mean...
: She’s caught up on you.
: ...What?
: Ever since you went into that coma thing, she’s been...obsessively looking into what could have caused it.
: She’s scoured like, every single poem your niece has ever written. To the point where even I’ve memorized a few of them. And she’s starting to sound like some kind of...conspiracy theorist.
: And, you know...I thought you coming out of that would have put an end to it. And I’d get my normal- well...normal-ish girlfriend back once you were alive again. But that’s not the case at all.
: Almost nothing’s changed. She’s still spending almost every night trying to put things together and...it’s getting to the point where I’m not sure how to handle it.
: Just walking away and leaving her to it isn’t cutting it, obviously. But you know me. I’m not assertive when it comes to her. And when I try to be, she just makes me feel like I don’t get it.
: And what do you want me to do about this?
: I don’t know. Would it kill you to maybe, like...talk to her? Or tell her that things are okay so she doesn’t spend the next decade trying to fix the same thing you are?
: I have.
: What do you mean you have? When? She told me she hadn’t seen you apart from the one day at school.
: Before I disappeared.
: She’s been poking her nose somewhere it doesn’t belong for a while now. And I told her how uncomfortable it made me, which led to her apologizing shortly after.
: But I was under the impression she dropped it by now. Not that she planned on dragging Ami into it as well.
: Fuck...
: Yeah. Sorry to disappoint you.
: No, it’s not that. You didn’t do anything wrong. She can...be like this sometimes.
: Wakana might seem straight-laced and “by the book” when it comes to school and whatnot. But when there’s something she can’t understand, she throws herself at it. Hard. And recklessly.
: But most of the time, she’s able to figure it out.
: But not this time.
: Like, she’s gone as far as theorizing that Ami might have known this was going to happen. Or that she wanted it to. But, like...why? Don’t you guys have a good relationship?
: I think “codependent” is the best word for our relationship.
: Is it? Because that’s not exactly a good word for any relationship.
: Maybe not for most people, but it works for us.
: She lost her parents at a very young age and I’ve been her guardian ever since. But I was a wreck back then, so it was more like her taking care of me.
: Which is why it’s so important that I keep an eye on her now since I’m finally getting a chance to be there as more than I actually am.
: If you want to know why I haven’t just ended it already and why I keep half-jokingly asking you to do it, it’s because of that. It’s because of her.
: If I’m gone, she’ll have no one.
: For the first time ever...I feel like I have a purpose.
: It’s just unfortunate that purpose showed up at the same time the rest of my world broke apart.
: Ami’s the ledge I’m hanging onto now. And yeah, I could let go. That’d be way easier than pulling myself up, after all.
: But I’d fall knowing that she’d jump in after me. And that is what I’m most afraid of.
: She doesn’t deserve to suffer over the choices I’ve made. She’s worked hard and deserves a good life.
: She’s just broken.
: And if Wakana is going to keep going through her poetry and invading her privacy by dissecting her most personal feelings-
: Sorry to interrupt, but...is that really what they are?
: What?
: Personal feelings.
: Do you know for sure that’s what she’s writing about?
: I mean...what else would it be? That’s what I taught her to-
: That’s...
: But when did I-
: Well, like...without beating around the bush, what if she’s just taking after her mom? And doing what she did?
: The Girl Who Cannot Breathe or whatever. That’s her, right? Because I’ve heard basically everything she’s ever written now thanks to Wakana and-
: Don’t talk about her.
: But-
: No one can do what she did.
: No one will ever see anything the way she did.
: I’m just trying to say that-
: If Ami is mimicking anyone, it’s me. And I’m done talking about this. So either drop it, or finish your lunch alone. Pick one.
: What did she do to you, man?
: I have to get home. Ami’s waiting.
: You’re the “Boy,” right?! The one she always wrote about?! That was you! Wasn’t it?!
: She can’t hurt you anymore...
: It’s over.
: No it’s not.
Osako’s affection has increased by 10! But maybe it's just pity!
When you get home, you check on your niece. She’s still asleep.
Your phone vibrates again. It’s a number you’ve yet to save and an apology you will not read.
As you fight against your inhibitions and punch the name “Osako Osaka” into your contacts, you remember what she said at the diner.
About how she can’t hurt you anymore.
And you know it’s not true.
Because when you climb into bed that night, she’s right there beside you — making circles on your chest with her index fingernail.
And while you can’t feel anything, you remember the sharp sting of when she bit it too short one night and drew blood while making these same exact circles.
They seemed so much bigger back then.
You imagine they would fit around your ankle.
Akira Arakawa’s [[DEPRESSION] has worsened!
He has learned [[GREATER FACADE]!
